title: A novel map of human p53 response elements uncovers evidence of selection pressures and variants similar to Li-Fraumeni Syndrome mutations
authors: Zhang P; Brown K; Barnes D; Kitchen-Smith I; Sims D; Flanagan A; De Noon S; Van Loo P; Hargreaves S; Cross W; Pillay N; Jafri M; Wallis Y; Ucanok D; Ntaoulas S; Manz MG; Tebaldi T; Inga A; Grochola LF; Bond G
one_liner_zh: 该文整合基因组图谱和测序数据绘制人类p53响应元件图谱，研究其选择压力与突变，虽涉及TF-DNA结合位点但以基因组学分析为主，缺乏AI或物理模拟建模方法。
abstract:
Background

The advent of functional genomic techniques and next generation sequencing has improved the characterization of the non-protein coding regions of the genome. However, the integration of these data into clinical practice is still in its infancy. Fifty percent of cancers mutate TP53 , which promotes tumorigenesis, in part, by inhibiting its ability to bind to non-coding regions of the genome and function as a sequence-specific transcription factor. P53 is a tumour suppressor that inhibits cell survival through regulating transcription of anti-survival genes. However, p53 also regulates transcription of pro-survival genes and the target gene(s) responsible for p53 tumour suppression remains an open topic of research.

Methods

In this study, we integrate detailed genome-wide maps of p53 responsive elements (p53-RE), p53 occupancy, recently defined candidate cis-Regulatory Elements (cCREs) and whole genome sequencing for cancers to better define the regions of the genome that harbour functional p53 enhancers.

Results

We determine that p53-REs are more likely to be closer to the consensus binding site, to be evolutionarily conserved and to be occupied by p53 in cellulo , when they reside in regions of the genome that have been noted to have accessible DNA and a regulatory epigenomic mark in at least one human cell even without obvious p53 activation signals (cCRE p53-REs). We offer evidence that it is only in cCRE p53-REs, where multiple signs of differential natural selection between pro-survival and anti-survival target genes can be noted. Using whole genome sequences of 38,377 individuals, we go on to demonstrate that carriers of rare germline mutations in cCRE p53-REs can have similar traits to carriers of rare p53 coding mutations that cause the Li-Fraumeni cancer predisposition syndrome.

Conclusions

Together, these observations suggest that functional p53 enhancers are enriched in cCREs and that germline mutations in them have the potential to improve current cancer risk management and screening strategies.
abstract_zh:
背景

功能基因组技术和下一代测序的出现，改善了对基因组非蛋白质编码区域的表征。然而，将这些数据整合到临床实践中仍处于起步阶段。50%的癌症会使TP53发生突变，这在一定程度上通过抑制其与基因组非编码区域结合并作为序列特异性转录因子发挥作用的能力，促进了肿瘤发生。P53是一种肿瘤抑制因子，通过调控抗生存基因的转录来抑制细胞存活。然而，p53也调控促生存基因的转录，而负责p53肿瘤抑制作用的靶基因仍是研究中的开放课题。

方法

在本研究中，我们整合了p53响应元件（p53-RE）的详细全基因组图谱、p53占据情况、近期定义的候选顺式调控元件（cCREs）以及癌症的全基因组测序，以更好地界定含有功能性p53增强子的基因组区域。

结果

我们确定，当p53-REs位于基因组中已被注意到在至少一种人类细胞中具有可及DNA和调控性表观基因组标记的区域时（即使没有明显的p53激活信号，即cCRE p53-REs），它们更可能接近共识结合位点、在进化上保守，并在细胞内被p53占据。我们提供证据表明，仅在cCRE p53-REs中，可以观察到促生存和抗生存靶基因之间多种差异自然选择的迹象。利用38,377个个体的全基因组序列，我们进一步证明，携带cCRE p53-REs中罕见种系突变的个体，可能具有与携带导致Li-Fraumeni癌症易感综合征的罕见p53编码突变个体相似的特征。

结论

综合这些观察结果表明，功能性p53增强子在cCREs中富集，并且其中的种系突变有潜力改善当前的癌症风险管理和筛查策略。
